thesis.title: HISTORICAL PRELIMINARY — HOOD Q3 2024 top-line YoY screen pass (single-rule, SEC-only)
thesis.thesis: HISTORICAL PRELIMINARY CANDIDATE — NOT AN INVESTMENT VIEW. On 2024-10-30 Robinhood Markets, Inc. [HOOD] reported Q3 2024 (period ended 2024-09-30) total net revenues of USD 637 million, up 36% YoY as reported by the issuer, clearing the frozen adapter's single rule (issuer-reported top-line revenue YoY >= 20%). This is a one-rule screen pass on a historical disclosure, not evidence of an attractive investment, and it carries no price or valuation input. The research question is whether the Q3 2024 revenue growth was driven by durable, repeatable engagement and monetization rather than by a crypto-linked revenue spike and a favorable expense comparison.
assumptions: Issuer-reported total net revenues of USD 637 million for Q3 2024 (period ended 2024-09-30) are the top-line basis; the issuer's own label is 'total net revenues', not gross revenue, and no other metric is substituted for the 20% threshold.
The reported 36% YoY top-line growth is taken as disclosed by the issuer in the Q3 2024 release; no independent recalculation of the prior-year base is performed here.
Transaction-based revenues of USD 319 million are a material share of the USD 637 million top line, so the durability of the growth depends on transaction activity persisting rather than reverting.
The reported 10% YoY decline in operating expenses is treated as a disclosed comparison, not as proof of a structural cost reset.
catalysts: Subsequent issuer disclosures that show whether crypto revenues and transaction-based revenues held at or above Q3 2024 levels.
Disclosure of engagement/monetization metrics that would indicate whether transaction-based revenue is repeatable rather than episodic.
invalidations: Issuer disclosure showing Q3 2024 total net revenues were restated or that the 36% YoY figure was not computed on a matched prior-year top-line basis.
Evidence that the YoY growth was predominantly a base-effect artifact (e.g., an unusually depressed prior-year quarter) rather than current-period strength.
Evidence that crypto revenues (USD 61 million, reported +165% YoY) and transaction-based revenues reversed sharply in the following period, undermining the durability premise.

evidence.note: Issuer top-line label is 'total_net_revenues'; YoY reported by issuer, not recomputed here.
Counterpoint field: prior-year quarter carried a USD 104 million regulatory accrual versus USD 10 million in Q3 2024.

evidence.boundary: No share price, market capitalization, valuation multiple, analyst target, or forward return is present in this packet or used in this thesis. The screen's excluded_dimensions list share_price, valuation, analyst_target, future_return, and current_market_data. Any valuation conclusion is out of scope and unsupported.

evidence.counterpoint: The most material counterpoint from a different supplied field is the regulatory accrual line: USD 104 million in Q3 2023 versus USD 10 million in Q3 2024. A USD 94 million swing in this single expense line is large relative to the USD 150 million of Q3 2024 net income and to the reported 10% YoY decline in operating expenses. This means the profit and expense improvement in the quarter is partly a comparison against a prior-year quarter burdened by a one-time regulatory charge, and the reported 36% top-line growth does not by itself establish that earnings power improved structurally. This is a counterpoint to the durability of the result, not a refutation of the disclosed revenue growth.

evidence.question: In the next issuer disclosure, do transaction-based revenues (USD 319 million) and crypto revenues (USD 61 million, +165% YoY) hold at or above Q3 2024 levels, and does operating expense growth stay negative once the USD 104 million prior-year regulatory accrual is no longer in the comparison base? A 'yes' to both would support durable monetization; a 'no' would indicate the Q3 2024 result was substantially crypto-cycle and base-effect driven.

message.content:
# HOOD — Historical SEC-Disclosure Candidate Research (single-rule screen)

## 1. Screen outcome: RETAINED (1 passed, 0 rejected)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Symbol / company | HOOD — Robinhood Markets, Inc. |
| Reporting period | Q3 2024, ended 2024-09-30 |
| Release date | 2024-10-30 |
| Criterion | Issuer-reported top-line revenue YoY ≥ 20.0% |
| Result | **Passed** — reported +36% YoY |
| Source URL | https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783879/000178387924000295/q32024robinhoodexhibit991.htm |
| Full SHA-256 | `27ba615060da18f74984973ec4c16a5a67f6215b2d3d91648c375f1192f3c973` |
| Failed criteria | None |
| Locator | "Third Quarter Results" revenue and expense bullets |

**Reported fields (USD million unless noted):** total net revenues 637; top-line YoY +36% (reported); net income 150; transaction-based revenues 319; crypto revenues 61 (+165% YoY reported); operating expenses YoY −10%; regulatory accrual 10 (Q3 2024) vs 104 (Q3 2023).

**Metric basis and units:** the issuer's own top-line label is **`total_net_revenues`**, not gross revenue. The adapter's own basis warning states that issuer labels differ (total revenue vs. total net revenues) and that only each issuer's own YoY disclosure or a matched prior-year top-line calculation may be applied. The 36% figure is taken as issuer-reported; I did not recompute the prior-year base.

**Adapter caveats:** this is a frozen offline SEC-source adapter (fixture `FINTECH-SEC-SCREEN-HOLDOUT-v1`), explicitly **not live market data** and not a contemporaneous peer ranking. `require_complete=false` was used, so completeness was not enforced; reported completeness 0.9762 with no flags. Packet omissions are not SEC filing omissions.

## 2. Independent counterpoint (different supplied field)

The most material counterpoint comes from the **regulatory accrual** line, not from the revenue line: **USD 104 million in Q3 2023 versus USD 10 million in Q3 2024** — a USD 94 million swing. That is large relative to the USD 150 million of Q3 2024 net income and to the reported 10% YoY decline in operating expenses. It implies the quarter's expense and profit improvement is partly a comparison against a prior-year quarter burdened by a one-time regulatory charge, so the +36% top-line growth does not by itself establish structurally improved earnings power. This qualifies the durability of the result; it does not refute the disclosed revenue growth.

A secondary tension worth noting: transaction-based revenues (319) are roughly half of the 637 top line, and crypto revenues grew +165% YoY — so the growth mix leans on activity-linked revenue that is inherently cyclical.

## 3. Saved thesis

Exactly one **HISTORICAL PRELIMINARY** candidate thesis was saved: `th_73239aeb76974fdd981e`, status `researching`, conviction 2, version 1. It carries the full source URL and SHA-256 in structured evidence, the key numbers above, the counterpoint, a discriminating follow-up question, and an explicit missing price/valuation boundary. `next_review_at` was omitted (no genuinely future-dated review was warranted).

**Discriminating follow-up question:** In the next issuer disclosure, do transaction-based revenues (319) and crypto revenues (61, +165% YoY) hold at or above Q3 2024 levels, and does operating expense growth stay negative once the USD 104 million prior-year regulatory accrual is no longer in the comparison base?

## 4. Explicit boundaries

- **No price or valuation input exists in this packet.** The screen's `excluded_dimensions` list share_price, valuation, analyst_target, future_return, and current_market_data. No valuation conclusion is drawn or supported.
- **Passing this one rule is not evidence of an attractive investment.** It is a single historical top-line growth test on one issuer's own disclosure.
- No trades, no live market tools, no cross-issuer ranking on a common date.
- No claim is made that anything absent from this packet was absent from the SEC filing.
